# The enumerated shape corpus — labelled from the definition, before any rule ran.
#
# GENERATED by itinerary_shape_corpus_test.go. Do not hand-edit: run
#   UPDATE_SHAPE_CORPUS=1 go test ./... -run TestEnumeratedCorpusFixtureIsCurrent
#
# WHY IT IS GENERATED. The interleave rule (runs A,B,A,B) scored 0 false
# rejections and 0 misses against a corpus written by the agent that wrote the
# rule, after earlier candidates had failed. That is an output of the rule, not
# evidence about it, and a second agent inventing more shapes carries the same
# bias. So nothing here was invented: every ENUM row is one cell of a full
# cross-product, and every label comes from the definition of a correct
# itinerary rather than from any rule's verdict.
#
# THE DEFINITION, which is the whole instrument:
#   A correct itinerary is a sequence of stays. Once you leave A for B you are
#   in B until you leave B.
# Read as two obligations and nothing more: (1) within a stay the days never
# step backwards, and (2) the stays' day intervals are ordered and do not
# overlap — a later stay may BEGIN on the day an earlier one ENDS (the shared
# transition day) but not before. It has no opinion on how many stays a city
# gets, and none on whether a traveler would plausibly book the trip.
#
# THE ENUMERATION: every run pattern up to 5 runs with no two adjacent runs
# sharing a hub (1 runs: 1 · 2 runs: 1 · 3 runs: 2 · 4 runs: 5 · 5 runs: 15), crossed with
# 2 run sizes × 8 day assignments × 2 content relations, deduplicated.
#
# NOT enumerated, said plainly rather than left to be assumed: hubless items,
# day_trip_from spellings, diacritic/case variance and patterns of six runs or
# more. The first three are hub SPELLINGS rather than run patterns and are
# carried by the KNOWN block (LEGIT-04/-05/-08); the fourth is the depth the
# ticket set.
#
# BLOCKS. KNOWN rows are the shapes the trip-scope-guard lane already worked
# from, transcribed so this corpus is a superset and the old numbers stay
# comparable. `new=yes` marks an ENUM row whose signature — the tuple of every
# structural fact a rule or the label can read — no KNOWN row presents.
#
# COLUMNS (tab separated):
#   id · block · new · pattern · runsize · days · content · label · reason · signature · items
#
# TOTALS: 589 shapes — 437 legal, 152 illegal; 18 KNOWN (15 distinct signatures), 571 enumerated, of which 563 are new.
#
